title: Symbols and advanced types (overview)
learningObjectives: Explain symbols and advanced types (overview) and use the relevant JavaScript language feature correctly.

understand.concept: Symbol() creates a unique primitive value often used as a property key. Well-known symbols such as Symbol.iterator customise language protocols. BigInt represents integers beyond the safe integer range of Number, and typeof has special cases such as typeof null returning 'object'.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding these primitives helps when reading advanced libraries and language APIs. They solve specific problems and should be chosen only when their semantics are needed.
understand.analogy: A Symbol is a unique tag; BigInt is an integer type designed for values larger than Number can represent safely.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript language protocols, primitive identity, and date/time semantics are defined by the language and runtime.

explain.narrative: The two symbols are distinct even with the same description. BigInt arithmetic uses the n suffix, and typeof null demonstrates a historical language quirk.

examples.explanation: The two symbols are distinct even with the same description. BigInt arithmetic uses the n suffix, and typeof null demonstrates a historical language quirk.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the behaviour described in the lesson.

practise.guidedTask: Create two symbols with the same description and compare them. Calculate with BigInt and explain why Number and BigInt should not be mixed implicitly.
practise.independentTask: Build a small example that uses this feature with normal inputs and edge cases. Explain when this feature is preferable to a simpler alternative.
hints: Read the return value and iteration protocol carefully.
Test duplicate, invalid, and boundary values.
Avoid assuming locale or time-zone output is identical everywhere.

questions.prompt: Are two Symbol('id') values equal just because their descriptions match?
options: No, each Symbol() call creates a unique value
questions.answer: No, each Symbol() call creates a unique value
questions.explanation: Symbol values are unique; their descriptions are for debugging and do not determine identity.

questions.prompt: What is a good practice when using advanced JavaScript features?
options: Understand their semantics and test edge cases
Use them everywhere regardless of need
questions.answer: Understand their semantics and test edge cases
questions.explanation: Advanced features are most useful when their specific semantics solve a real problem.
